title: Strong subadditivity of topological entropy on the torus: Rényi order and non-Abelian structure
abstract: We classify strong subadditivity for the canonical topological Rényi functional at finite positive orders on an unpunctured torus in the topological quantum field theory of any finite unitary modular tensor category. Universal validity means validity for all pure ground states and all regular region pairs with transverse or disjoint boundaries and compatible corner rounding. At von Neumann order one, the inequality holds universally. For each fixed order strictly between zero and one, universal validity is equivalent to pointedness, meaning that every simple anyon type has quantum dimension one. For every nonpointed category and each finite positive order other than one, we construct a violating pure state and an allowed pair. For a fixed pointed category and fixed order above one, universal validity is equivalent to a same-order modular Fourier entropy bound for every pure state. Global homological constraints on actual unions and intersections and established weighted modular uncertainty prove the order-one theorem. For parallel annuli at fixed flux distribution, the order-one functional is affine in their positive count. At other orders, unequal quantum dimensions on the occupied support induce strict curvature that suitable overlapping regions convert into negative deficits. Under the boundary-charge cutting prescription, the von Neumann theorem extends to arbitrary logical density matrices in the same ground space.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the strong subadditivity property for a topological entanglement entropy functional defined on a torus within TQFT. It establishes that this property holds universally only at the von Neumann order ($\alpha=1$). For other orders, the validity of the inequality is strictly constrained by algebraic properties of the underlying quantum system, such as whether the anyon types have unit quantum dimension.
main_problem: The paper classifies the conditions under which the canonical topological Rényi functional exhibits strong subadditivity on an unpunctured torus, and how this depends on the Rényi order ($\alpha$).
main_result: Strong subadditivity holds universally at the von Neumann order ($\alpha=1$), but for $0 < \alpha < 1$, it is equivalent to the underlying modular tensor category being pointed.
method: The analysis uses replica constructions, Mayer-Vietoris surface constraints, and comparisons to established entropy inequalities to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the subadditivity to hold.
model_or_system: The theory is set within the framework of Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) associated with a finite unitary modular tensor category ($\mathcal{C}$), applied to entanglement on an unpunctured torus ($T^2$).
key_observables: Topological Rényi functional ($	ext{Stop}_\alpha$), quantum dimensions ($d_a$) of simple anyons, and the strong subadditivity inequality itself.
important_parameters: The Rényi order $\alpha$, which dictates the mathematical constraints; the structure of the modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis initially focuses on pure ground states, though it extends the result to arbitrary logical density matrices using the boundary-charge cutting prescription.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure suggests derivations involving topological constraints on subsurfaces (e.g., annuli on the torus).
paper_structure: The paper develops by defining the functional, proving the $\alpha=1$ case, classifying the general $\alpha$-dependence (linking it to pointedness for $0 < \alpha < 1$), and finally extending the results to mixed states.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical classification of entanglement inequalities based on the underlying algebraic structure (modular tensor category) provides deep insights into the nature of quantum correlations beyond standard thermal or geometric considerations.
